# Worldbuilding

Curated by Skill Harbor — a world-architect skill for fiction writers and game designers: magic and technology system design (Sanderson's Laws), cultural and societal architecture that avoids monocultures, historical timelines built on cause and effect, geography and climate logic, religions people would actually believe, economies, naming languages, and world bibles. Its philosophy is the "one big lie" principle — ask the audience to accept one departure from reality, then be ruthlessly consistent about every implication — and the iceberg rule: show 10%, hint at 90%. Grounded in companion reference files for creation patterns, failure diagnosis ("sharp edges"), and validation rules. Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @omer-metin. Honest caveats: persona-driven with a strong opinionated voice ("world architect" who has made every mistake); depends on the companion reference files (patterns.md, sharp_edges.md, validations.md) that must ship with the skill; fiction and games only — not for technical documentation. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
